note: Liver-directed AAV delivery of B-domain-deleted FVIII; valoctocogene's pivotal package was F8/Rag2-knockout mice plus cynomolgus macaques, while haemophilia A dogs (canine FVIII, AAV2/6/8/9) were the field's durability and tolerance model.
label: Haemophilia A (FVIII gene therapy)

engagement.note: AAV2 heavy/light-chain vectors into F8-knockout mice gave dose-dependent, therapeutic-to-supraphysiologic FVIII after portal-vein injection.
engagement.quote: After intraportal vein injection of these vectors in hemophilia-A mice, therapeutic to superphysiologic levels of active FVIII were achieved in plasma in a dose-dependent manner.
engagement.confidence: medium (abstract only; no PMC full text)

engagement.note: BMN 270 (valoctocogene) gave dose-dependent liver transduction and plasma hFVIII-SQ in knockout mice; two macaques per dose expressed similar levels until anti-hFVIII antibodies.
engagement.short: BMN 270 expresses FVIII in mice, macaques
engagement.quote: Comparable doses in primates produced similar levels of circulating FVIII.

engagement.note: Liver biopsies 2.6-4.1 years after valoctocogene showed hepatocyte transduction, full-length circular episomes and FVIII-SQ RNA with the same dose trends as mice and macaques.
engagement.quote: In both humans and animals, there were dose-dependent trends in the numbers of hepatocytes transduced with vector genomes, in quantities of circular full-length/ITR-fused vector genomes, and in expression of FVIII-SQ RNA.
engagement.judgement: Only five biopsied participants, all from the phase 1/2 study, and the animal data are BioMarin's own; but the comparison is explicit and tissue-level, so it sets 'same'.

dose.note: Mouse dose-response was the class's exposure model; dogs received lower doses of canine FVIII and were never dose-matched to patients.
dose.quote: After intraportal vein injection of these vectors in hemophilia-A mice, therapeutic to superphysiologic levels of active FVIII were achieved in plasma in a dose-dependent manner.
dose.confidence: medium (abstract only; no PMC full text)

dose.note: Mice reached 380% FVIII at steady state; phase 1/2 patients plateaued at 104%: BioMarin's own 3.7-fold mouse-to-human drop.
dose.quote: This results in approximately 3.7-fold drop of FVIII expression of BMN 270 from mouse to human.
dose.judgement: Judgement call: the direction held (therapeutic FVIII at 6e13 vg/kg) but the exposure target did not, and the lower human doses (6e12, 2e13 vg/kg) stayed at <=3 IU/dL (Rangarajan 2017, 10.1056/NEJMoa1708483), so the clinical dose was found by escalation, not from the mouse. Macaques (n=2/dose, 1e13 and 3.6e13) lost expression to anti-hFVIII antibodies within weeks and could not set a target. Downgrade to 'untested' if a 3.7-fold species gap is read as scaling rather than a miss.

efficacy.note: AAV2-canine-FVIII to dog liver gave 2-4% FVIII sustained beyond 14 months with partial correction of clotting and cuticle bleeding times.
efficacy.quote: The use of this vector for hepatic gene transfer in a canine model of hemophilia A resulted in the sustained (> 14 months) expression of biologically active FVIII.
efficacy.confidence: medium (abstract only; no PMC full text)

efficacy.note: Dogs held FVIII 10 years; valoctocogene recipients lost about half their expression from year 1 to 2; SPK-8011 stayed stable in 12 of 16.
efficacy.quote: These results were unexpected given observations … from studies in large-animal models of hemophilia A that showed durable factor VIII transgene-derived expression for 10 years.
efficacy.confidence: high (full text via PMC8672712); quote elided with an ellipsis from a 48-word sentence
efficacy.judgement: Bleeding fell in every trial as the dogs predicted (>90% fewer bleeds over 24 dog-years, Sabatino 2011, 10.1038/mt.2010.240); durability split by product. The dog matched SPK-8011 (George 2021) but valoctocogene declined year on year (Pasi 2020, 10.1056/NEJMoa1908490; Mahlangu 2023, 10.1056/NEJMoa2211075), and contra overrides. Caveat: the dogs received canine FVIII at ~1e13 vg/kg (Nguyen 2021, 10.1038/s41587-020-0741-7; Batty 2022, 10.1182/blood.2021014735), never the clinical products, and valoctocogene's own mice/macaques were silent on multi-year durability.

safety.note: Macaques at up to 3.6e13 vg/kg and mice at up to 2e14 showed no ALT/AST rise, no hepatocyte ER stress and no apoptosis.
safety.short: No ALT rise, no ER stress in animals
safety.quote: All monkeys developed anti-AAV5 antibodies post-dosing, and no elevation of plasma ALT or AST levels was observed throughout the study.

safety.note: Patient hepatocytes expressing hFVIII-SQ showed no GRP78/ER stress, fibrosis or inflammation; the mouse GRP78-FVIII relationship held in participants.
safety.short: Patient livers: no ER stress, like mice
safety.quote: Indeed, endogenous liver GRP78 levels appear to correlate with circulating hFVIII-SQ protein levels in mice, as well as in the three participants with detectable plasma FVIII activity in our study.
safety.confidence: medium (full text via PMC9018415, but the match covers ER stress only, in five biopsies)
safety.reason: ER stress matched; ALT rise never compared
safety.judgement: Narrow match. The dominant clinical safety event, ALT elevation in 81% of phase 3 patients with 87% needing immunosuppression (FDA SBRA 2023, https://www.fda.gov/media/170455/download), was absent in macaques (Bunting 2018), and the mouse cardiac necrosis/mortality at >=6.5e13 vg/kg in the FDA toxicology studies never appeared in patients; no primary source states either comparison (checked SBRA, clinical review memo, pharmacology-toxicology and clinical pharmacology reviews), so neither can set 'contra'. Dog tolerance (no inhibitors, Sabatino 2011) matched 'No subjects developed an inhibitor to FVIII' (SBRA) but is likewise uncompared in print.
